title: The init-wizard test family times out intermittently in CI, on both ubuntu and windows, and blocks unrelated PRs
summary:
Tests in test/init.test.ts that spawn a process and wait on TTY behaviour intermittently time out in the required 'lint - typecheck - test' job. Seen on both platforms, at both configured timeouts, naming different tests each time:

- 2026-09-11, PR #6, windows-latest: 'cli - init dispatch > the router wires stdinIsTTY + stderrIsTTY + a fake prompter through to the wizard end-to-end (LORE-260)' timed out at 60000ms. It passed on one SHA and failed on the next, where the only difference was a .quest/completed/*.json file.
- 2026-09-15, promotion PR #91, ubuntu-latest: THREE init.test.ts wizard cases (Hermes, Antigravity/Gemini, AGENTS.md-label) each timed out at exactly 10000ms, on a commit that changed only .quest/tasks/*.json, CHANGELOG.md and docs/log.md.
- 2026-09-15, PR #105, ubuntu-latest, run 34984200004 job 104431984958: 'the interactive wizard offers Hermes only when its executable is detected' timed out at 10002.65ms. 3056 pass, 1 fail. The identical source tree had passed that exact job minutes earlier on run 34983645053; the only delta was two .quest JSON files. Cleared on re-run.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A RECORD AND NOT JUST A RE-RUN: it is a flaky REQUIRED check, so every occurrence blocks an unrelated PR until a human notices and re-runs it. Three occurrences are on the books and the judgement that they were flakes rather than regressions has so far lived only in a session's private memory - meaning each new session pays to re-derive it, and one that gets it wrong either bisects a phantom regression or, worse, reports a red job as passing.

THE COMMON THREAD IS NOT ONE TEST OR ONE OS. An earlier version of the rule said 'if it fails on ubuntu too, or names a different test, it is real' - both happened at once and it was still a flake. What actually decides it is the tree: does the diff touch anything the failing test exercises, and did the same tree already pass this job? Two noes mean flake, on any platform.

A 60s timeout on a TTY-wizard test is the shape of a test waiting on something the runner delivers slower, not of a test that is wrong - so raising the number again is the tempting fix and probably the wrong one.

Related: LCLI-491 tracks a different timeout flake (Ladybug projection-lifecycle at 5000ms). Two timeout flakes in required checks may share a cause - runner contention rather than two independent test bugs - and are worth looking at together.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The root cause is identified: why init-wizard tests that spawn a process and wait on TTY behavior intermittently exceed their timeout on a CI runner but not locally
The fix removes the flake rather than raising the timeout, or the timeout increase is justified in writing as the correct model of the work the test does
A re-run of the affected job is no longer part of the normal delivery path for an unrelated diff
The rule for judging one of these failures - does the diff reach the test, and did the same tree already pass this job - is recorded in the repository rather than only in a session's memory

implementationNotes:
A THIRD timeout flake in this repository's CI, in a third subsystem — evidence for the shared-cause question this task and LCLI-491 raise, not a fourth independent bug.

2026-09-15, PR #107, run 34990665392, job 104454157305: 'explorer browser qualification (chromium · firefox · webkit)' failed with

    [webkit] > test/browser/explorer.pw.ts:34:1 > KBD-01 and SR-01 provide complete keyboard and semantic detail flows
    Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded while setting up "page".

17 passed, 1 failed. The SAME test passed on chromium and firefox in the same run, and the failure is in page SETUP — browser launch — not in an assertion about content.

WHY IT IS A FLAKE, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ON THE USUAL 'same tree passed already' TEST, WHICH WAS NOT AVAILABLE: this was the branch's first run, so there was no earlier green on the identical tree to appeal to. The diff-reachability half was decisive instead. The PR changes ci.yml, .lore/config.toml (a [reconcile.overrides] entry), two test files and one .quest record. test/browser/explorer.pw.ts builds every artifact it renders from FIXTURES — loadSmallExplorerFixture, buildLargeExplorerFixture, test/fixtures/snapshot/v1.json — never from this repository's own docs bundle or its .lore config. A reconcile override cannot reach it. Confirmed by re-run.

THE PATTERN NOW HAS THREE MEMBERS, all 'a test times out' in a required or near-required check, all in code that spawns a process or a browser and waits on it:
  - init-wizard TTY tests (this task): 10000ms and 60000ms, ubuntu and windows
  - Ladybug projection-lifecycle (LCLI-491): 5000ms
  - Playwright webkit page setup (here): 30000ms

Three subsystems, three timeout values, one shape. That is stronger evidence for runner contention or a shared resource limit than for three unrelated test bugs, and it is the reason to investigate the three together before fixing any of them in isolation. Raising a timeout is the tempting fix in all three and is probably wrong in all three.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS: this repo's ci.yml sets concurrency cancel-in-progress for pull_request. A re-run of the failed job (gh run rerun <id> --failed) reuses the run and is safe, but pushing a new commit to measure something cancels the in-flight run — which matters when a gate proof needs two runs on two SHAs.

A FOURTH occurrence, and this one names a likely root cause AND a defect in the guard that already exists for it.

2026-09-15, PR #107, run 34991819837, job 104458113048, ubuntu-latest: the whole test leg HUNG and was killed by its own wrapper. Not an individual test timeout -- 'Process completed with exit code 124', the 'timeout --kill-after=10s 6m' guard firing. The last group opened was test/agent-workflow-adapter.test.ts, which spawns the lore CLI as a real subprocess with spawnSync and reads its stdout/stderr.

NOT REACHABLE BY THE DIFF: that file builds its own fixture bundle in a mkdtemp directory and never reads this repository's CLAUDE.md or .quest. The delta from the previous SHA was CLAUDE.md's managed-block version line and three .quest records, and the previous SHA passed this exact job. Two noes, so: flake. Confirmed by re-run, which went green.

THE GUARD FOR THIS ALREADY EXISTS AND DID NOT FIRE, which is the actual finding. .github/workflows/ci.yml's ubuntu leg carries a documented retry:

    # Bun 1.3.14 can race Linux epoll registration when isolated files
    # concurrently construct streams over the process stdio fds.

It retries ONCE, but only when the log contains the literal 'error: EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl'. This run produced no such line -- it hung instead -- so lore_bun_status was 124, the grep missed, and the job failed outright.

So the guard is keyed on ONE FACE of the race. The same mechanism can present as an EEXIST error (retried) or as a hang (not retried, killed at 6m, red). A guard that recognises only the noisy failure mode leaves the quiet one looking like a real regression, which is exactly the cost this task was filed for.

THIS ALSO SPLITS THE FAMILY, and the split matters more than the count:
  - EXPLAINED by the Bun epoll/stdio race: agent-workflow-adapter (spawnSync over stdio) and the init-wizard TTY tests. Both construct streams over process stdio fds under file isolation.
  - NOT explained by it: the Playwright webkit page-setup timeout, which is a browser launch, and possibly Ladybug projection-lifecycle. Do not fold these in on the strength of sharing the word 'timeout'.

That correction matters because 'four timeouts, one cause' is the tempting story and it is probably wrong. Two causes, one of which is named and already half-handled, is the better hypothesis to test.

CHEAPEST REAL FIX, and it is not raising a timeout: widen the existing retry's trigger to include the bounded-timeout exit (124) as well as the EEXIST string, so the known race is retried in both its forms. That is a change to a guard that already has a comment explaining the mechanism -- the judgement is already written down, it is just keyed too narrowly.

Verified AC1 against the current file (not just the note's line numbers): the ubuntu leg's retry guard is now at .github/workflows/ci.yml lines ~131-150 pre-edit (matches the task note's cited 131-148 closely enough to confirm no drift-of-mechanism), and the mechanism is exactly as described -- grep -Fq only on the literal EEXIST string, missing the exit-124 bounded-timeout-hang case.

AC2: widened the retry condition to 'grep ... || [[ "${lore_bun_status}" -eq 124 ]]'. Did NOT raise the 10000ms per-test timeout or the 6m/10s timeout/kill-after wrapper -- confirmed via git diff that only the if-condition and the warning message changed, timeout numbers are untouched.

AC3: test/ci-workflow.test.ts gained (a) a string-level assertion that the widened condition text is present in ci.yml's Test step, and (b) a new describe block 'ci.yml ubuntu Bun-epoll retry trigger (LCLI-507)' that extracts the real condition via regex from the loaded workflow and executes it in a real bash subshell (spawnSync) against fabricated log contents + exit codes, asserting retry fires for EEXIST-only, exit-124-only, and both, and does NOT fire for a genuine unrelated failure. Mutation-tested by hand: reverted the ci.yml condition to grep-only, re-ran -- both the string assertion and the exit-124 behavioral test failed as expected; restored and re-ran -- all 14 tests in the file pass. This is real executed evidence, not an inferred claim -- but it cannot prove the actual CI race won't recur, only that the widened trigger fires correctly for both known signals.

AC4: recorded the diff-reachability flake-judgment rule as a comment block in .github/workflows/ci.yml immediately before the 'Test' step (the retry guard's home), and a second comment inline in the ubuntu branch cross-referencing it. Checked docs/runbooks/ (index.md, agent-onboarding.md, lore-cli-handover.md, release-publishing.md, docker-e2e-testing-environment.md, backlog-json-patch.md, agent-profile-operation.md) -- none cover CI-flake-judgment territory, so per the task's own 'don't force it' instruction, did not create a new runbook or force this into an unrelated one. The ci.yml comment block is the recorded home.

Verified no conflict with LCLI-502's open work: no open PRs at task start (gh pr list --state open returned empty), and this task's files (.github/workflows/ci.yml, test/ci-workflow.test.ts) do not overlap scripts/publish-release.sh, test/publish-release-script.test.ts, or the release docs LCLI-502 was scoped to.

CORRECTION (independent reviewer finding, re-verified 2026-09-16 against real CI logs, not taken on the reviewer's word alone): AC1 and AC3 were checked prematurely. This task's title and its first three logged occurrences (PR #6 windows-latest 60000ms; PR #91 ubuntu-latest, three cases at 10000ms; PR #105 ubuntu-latest, one case at 10002.65ms) are a PER-TEST bun-test --timeout shape -- an individual test fails while the overall process finishes and reports a plain pass/fail count. Pulled the actual log for job 104431984958 (PR #105, run 34984200004 attempt 1) via 'gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/jobs/104431984958/logs --allow-escape-sequences': it shows 'this test timed out after 10000ms.' and ends with '##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.' -- exit 1, not 124, and NO 'error: EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl' or epoll text anywhere in the ~3800-line log. Neither the original guard nor this task's widened one (grep-match OR exit-124) can retry that shape. The delivered fix only and correctly addresses the FOURTH, later-diagnosed occurrence (test/agent-workflow-adapter.test.ts, a genuine whole-process hang, exit 124) -- which the task's own implementation notes already distinguish as a separate failure shape sharing only a suspected root cause. Uncheck AC1 (root cause identified) and AC3 (re-run no longer part of normal delivery) rather than reword them: the original wording still correctly states the unmet bar for the per-test-timeout family, and rewriting AC text after delivery to match only what shipped would understate what remains open. AC2 (fix does not raise timeouts) and AC4 (diff-reachability rule recorded) remain honestly checked -- both are unconditionally true regardless of this scope correction.

Filed LCLI-516 to track the still-open per-test-timeout family (PR #6, #91, #105, all in test/init.test.ts's TTY-wizard tests), referencing this task as prior art/related, so it is not silently dropped now that this task is Done.
finalSummary: Widened the ubuntu Bun-epoll retry guard in .github/workflows/ci.yml to trigger on exit 124 (the bounded-timeout hang) as well as the EEXIST string match, without raising either timeout. This resolves ONLY the whole-process-hang presentation of the race, demonstrated by test/agent-workflow-adapter.test.ts (job 104458113048, PR #107) -- confirmed by an independent review pass and re-verified directly against CI logs that the task's OWN original three occurrences (PR #6, #91, #105, all test/init.test.ts TTY-wizard tests) are a mechanistically different per-test bun-test --timeout shape (process exits 1 normally, no EEXIST, no exit 124) that this fix structurally cannot catch. AC1 and AC3 are correctly left unchecked for that reason. Follow-up tracked as LCLI-516. Added string-level and real bash-executed behavioral tests in test/ci-workflow.test.ts for the widened trigger, mutation-tested by hand. Recorded the diff-reachability flake-judgment rule as a comment block in ci.yml next to the retry guard; no existing docs/runbooks file covers this territory so none was forced. Delivered in PR #126 (https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/pull/126), branch fix/LCLI-507-widen-bun-retry-guard.
